title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 94–96). A 'disposition' E = (E, Σ_E) is a set E with a family Σ_E ⊂ P(E) of 'closed' subsets. The family is stable under arbitrary intersections, so it is a complete lattice. σ_E : E → Σ_E sends x to the smallest closed set containing x. The symbol written Ψ°_E / 'sup Ψ°' appears to be the closure (or polar) operator, so that 'sup Ψ°_{E'}(T)' is the closure in Σ_{E'} of a subset T.

Three descriptions of morphisms are compared:
- Corr(Σ, Σ'): maps α_* : Σ_E → Σ_{E'} commuting with arbitrary sups, i.e. morphisms of complete join-lattices.
- Corr(E, E'): set-valued maps α : E → Σ_{E'} ⊂ P(E'), with (a) every α(x) closed and (b) the conditions (iv) of an earlier proposition. These amount to α(y) ⊂ α(x) whenever y ∈ σ_E(x), i.e. compatibility with the specialisation preorder.
- Corr*(E, E'): relations R ⊂ E×E' whose rows R(x) are closed in E' and whose columns ᵗR(x') are closed in E.

The bijections are φ(α_*) = α_* ∘ σ_E and ψ(α) = {(x,x') | x' ∈ complement of α(x)}.

This page finishes the proof that φ is bijective. Let α_* be in Corr(Σ, Σ') and put α = φ(α_*).
- α_* is recovered from α by α_*(S) = sup_{x∈S} α(x). This holds because S = sup_{x∈S} σ_E(x) in Σ_E and α_* commutes with sups.
- Condition (iv b) holds for α. If y ∈ σ_E(x) then σ_E(y) ≤ σ_E(x), so α(y) = α_*σ_E(y) ≤ α_*σ_E(x) = α(x). Hence the closure of α(σ_E(x)) is contained in α(x). The reverse inclusion is trivial since x ∈ σ_E(x). qed.

11.7. Grothendieck then builds a category. Objects are dispositions. Morphisms E → E' are multivalued correspondences satisfying a), b) of p. 94. Composition is 'closure of the set-theoretic composite': β ∘_dis α = sup Ψ°_{E''}(β ∘_ens α). The identity is σ_E.

The next page states three things:
- This category is equivalent to that of complete lattices (the transcription's 'dérivateurs commutatifs / topos / topocosmos' is doubtful). Morphisms there are monotone maps commuting with sups, read 'in either direction', i.e. adjoint pairs.
- It carries an involutive self-duality that is the identity on objects and transposition on morphisms.
- Grothendieck draws an explicit analogy with Hilbert spaces and adjoint operators.

In modern terms this is the classical fact that the category of sup-lattices is equivalent to the category of closure spaces with 'closed' relations, and that Sup ≅ Sup^op via right adjoints. In the Corr* form these relations are exactly the 'bonds' between formal contexts.
errors: No mathematical error in the final argument; it is routine. Several crossed-out false starts appear (attempts with Ψ°_E(y) ≤ Ψ°_E(x), and a direct sup estimate) before settling on σ_E(y) ≤ σ_E(x).
The inserted fragment 'α_*(S − Ψ°_E(x))' near the formula S = sup σ_E(x) is a stray or garbled marginal insertion and is not mathematically meaningful as transcribed.
Only one inclusion (closure of α(σ_E(x)) ⊂ α(x)) is written; the reverse is left implicit (it is trivial).

ideas.what: Join-preserving maps between the lattices of closed sets correspond bijectively to closed-set-valued maps on points compatible with specialisation, via α_*(S) = sup_{x∈S} α(x)
ideas.modern_name: Free sup-lattice / join-dense generation by point closures; sup-lattice morphisms determined on generators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of lattice theory (Birkhoff, Raney 1950s); Joyal–Tierney 1984 for the categorical treatment

ideas.what: Closed relations R ⊂ E×E' with closed rows and columns, corresponding to sup-maps (Corr*)
ideas.modern_name: Bonds between formal contexts / Chu-space-like morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ganter–Wille (formal concept analysis, 1980s–1999); Barr/Pratt for Chu spaces

ideas.what: Category of dispositions with composition = closure of the relational composite, identities = closure maps σ_E
ideas.modern_name: Category of closure spaces with closed relations (a Kleisli/quotient of Rel), equivalent to Sup

ideas.what: Self-duality of this category: identity on objects, transposition on morphisms, with an analogy to Hilbert spaces and adjoint operators
ideas.modern_name: Sup ≅ Sup^op via adjoints; dagger / involutive categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Joyal–Tierney 1984 (Sup self-dual); dagger categories: Abramsky–Coecke 2004, Selinger 2007

missed.claim: Grothendieck (continuing onto the next page) explicitly frames the self-duality of complete lattices with transposed correspondences as analogous to Hilbert spaces with adjoint operators. This anticipates, in informal form, the dagger-category viewpoint later formalised in categorical quantum mechanics. It is a remark, not a construction, and the self-duality itself is classical.
missed.quote: Cette composition ... (next page: 'autodualité (involutive) ... la flèche transposée [Analogie avec les espaces de Hilbert ... opérateurs adjoints]')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor historical precursor note for dagger categories / Rel-type involutive categories. It is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page completes a routine lattice-theoretic verification and defines the standard category of closure spaces with closed relations, which is equivalent to self-dual Sup. All of this is classical (Joyal–Tierney, formal concept analysis bonds). The only mildly interesting element, the Hilbert-space/adjoint analogy, is on the next page and is informal.
transcription_corrections: 'satisfait aux conditions de page 4' should read 'page 94'.
The underbrace under α(x) in the α_* formula reads '∈ Σ_{E'}' (or similar), not 'idéal'.
'Or si y ∈ σ_E(x), on a σ_E(y) ≤ σ_E(x)' — the inserted correction above the line replaces the struck Ψ°-inequality.
The line '(iv b) sur α' reads approximately: 'ᾱ(σ_E(x)) et α(x) ont même ... = sup Ψ°_{E'}', i.e. compare the closure of α(σ_E(x)) with α(x).
In the composition formula, the struck term is 'β∘α', replaced by 'sup Ψ°_{E''}(β ∘_ens α)'.
